books.section: Topic 5.8 Military Conflict in the Civil War
Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

primary_sources: General Robert E. Lee, General Order No. 9 (April 10, 1865)

stimulus.source_note: General Robert E. Lee, General Order No. 9, April 10, 1865. Public domain. “. . .” marks omitted text.
stimulus.text:
“After four years of arduous service marked by unsurpassed courage and fortitude, the Army of Northern Virginia has been compelled to yield to overwhelming numbers and resources. . . . I need not tell the survivors of so many hard-fought battles, who have remained steadfast to the last, that I have consented to the result from no distrust of them.”

—General Robert E. Lee, General Order No. 9 (Farewell Address), April 10, 1865

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note

rationales.A: Lee blames overwhelming numbers and resources, praises his men, and says he does not distrust them.
rationales.B: Background: Lee surrendered his army and told his men to go home; he rejected guerrilla war.

rationales.general:
1. The document is a farewell from a defeated general to his own soldiers.
2. Its work is explanation: why we lost, and what your service meant.
3. Lee answers with arithmetic, not with blame: overwhelming numbers and resources.
4. A historian reads it as the losing side’s first draft of its own story.
Remember: a farewell address is evidence of how defeat is explained, not of what happens next.
